title: Financial marketing can transfer cost into application time and credit exposure before a remedy becomes visible
source_unit: Federal Trade Commission Credit Karma enforcement and refund-administration record; valid-claim recipients are a remedy-program population, not a representative credit applicant sample
geography: United States federal consumer-protection enforcement involving Credit Karma credit offers

observations.period: October 2024 initial refund distribution; April 2026 payment reissue route

denominator.unit: people with valid claims who requested compensation; recipient denominator not published on the checked page

aggregate_payment_distribution.unit: US dollars, more than, refunded in October 2024

time_and_credit_harm.value: people received pre-approved offers, applied, were sometimes denied, wasted time, and sometimes saw credit scores drop

reissue_method.value: Zelle payments to people who did not cash a check or accept PayPal

individual_time_loss_and_credit_recovery.value: not observed in the public refund page

observations.method: Official FTC refund-program page checked September 17, 2026; retain the aggregate refund total and reissue process as administrator-reported measures, not as an individual time-loss, credit-repair, or recovery rate.
observations.uncertainty: The page does not publish the valid-claim denominator, amount distribution, check-cashing rate, failed-delivery count, individual application sequence, score change, correction, alternative credit access, switching, trust, or later action.
observations.subgroup: People who filed valid claims after applying to qualifying Credit Karma offers; applicants, denied applicants, claimants, earlier payment recipients, and reissue recipients are distinct groups.
observations.counterinterpretation: A payment can compensate some time or financial harm without reversing a credit inquiry, restoring an opportunity that was missed, or changing how consumers evaluate or use credit-marketing platforms.

related_sources.claim: FTC lists Credit Karma Settlement as an active April 2026 refund program.

boundary: This record establishes reported deceptive credit-offer allegations, time and possible score harm, aggregate refund distribution, and a current reissue route. It does not establish individual exposure, score correction, receipt, restored credit access, trust, collective action, or exit.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: FTC Credit Karma refund HTML retrieved without retaining a repository copy
